channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [8] Single-crystalline CoSi semimetals with high conductivity and reliability
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Lain-Jong Li, Yang Chai

Authors: Jiewei Chen, Jianmin Yan, Lingwei Fan, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of CoSi, a known topological semimetal, with relevant electrical properties.

Tags: #topologicalsemimetal #CoSi #electricaltransport

Abstract: The electrical resistivity of conventional copper interconnects increases as their dimensions decrease. In contrast, the resistivity of CoSi nanoflakes decreases as their thickness is reduced from 1 μm to ∼20 nm. These nanoflakes demonstrate high reliability and serve as promising interconnects at the nanoscale.

item.title: [7] Electrically programmable polariton symmetry breaking via non-Hermitian dissipation engineering
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Hai Hu, Qing Dai

Authors: Na Chen, Hanchao Teng, Yifu Sun, et al.

Score 7/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Explores topological polaritons and symmetry breaking in real material heterostructures.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #polaritons #topology #heterostructures #2Dmaterials

Abstract: Reversible tuning of polariton topology in α-MoO3/aligned carbon nanotube heterostructures is achieved through gate-tunable anisotropic dissipation, with the aligned carbon nanotube layer operating as a momentum-space loss filter.
